`deletePrefixWholesale` reports `out_fully_drained = true` only when the LIST reaches its natural end; budget exhaustion reports false, and `pruneSupersededGenerations` advances `snap_pruned_through` only past fully drained prefixes.
The post-CAS generation-prefix hand-off uses a separate budget from ordinary prune work because it is a one-shot event whose only existing backstop after a partial reclaim is `fsck`.

The outcome-entry cap limits only the `GcOutcomes` audit-log PUT: `settleEntry` still removes spared entries from `still_retired`, and `CasGcRetiredSpared`, `GcRecheckVerdict`, and `forgetCondemnMarker` run even when the `OutcomeEntry` push is skipped.
The round-budget implementation introduces no persisted object kinds and no protocol-step changes; the budget is stack-local, and the one-pass round still commits `gc/state` exactly once.

`RefPlan::changedRows` and `shouldDeferRound` can defer an entire fold round based on a listed tail observation, but the defer path performs no destructive work, advances no coverage cursor, and is bounded by `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds`.

The `CaGcDestructiveGateCore` model pins `UniverseAuthoritative == TRUE` because it models the post-flip posture; production's not-yet-knowable-universe posture suppresses destructive work and is covered by `CasGcFrontierGate.HiddenPlusOneInAnUnknownNamespaceIsRefusedByTheProductionDefault`.

Normal rounds and healthy `REBUILD` apply every returned runtime retirement before downstream work and proceed only for `{Authoritative, DrainComplete}`; damaged-state `REBUILD` uses a no-parent, zero-catalog-mutation path.
The raw `cas_gc_maintenance_state` object at `gc/maintenance_state` stores only a bounded opaque janitor cursor and uses one materialized read followed by one expected-token or expected-absence CAS.
The maintenance-state codec requires `cur`, limits decoded cursors to 64 KiB, uses `FormatId::GcMaintenanceState = 25` with `{7, 7}` change points, and caps raw control objects at 512 KiB.
Maintenance-state `CORRUPTED_DATA` is classified as corrupt with its exact token, while future-version and backend failures propagate; CAS conflicts do not retry, reread, or adopt a winner.

The catalog-only pre-fold drain runs after lease acquisition against the authoritative adopted parent and before `DEFER`, the hot stream LIST, the successor catalog cut, fold, `REBUILD` adoption, or successor seal adoption.
A pre-fold deletion requires the complete exact `Removing` row, matching parent cleanup evidence, and no durable hold.

Full-catalog tokens require a serial rescan after every CAS outcome; for `N` eligible rows the drain costs one adopted-seal GET, at least `N+1` complete catalog GETs, and `N` exact catalog CASes, plus retries for conflict or ambiguity.

Healthy `REBUILD` drains before taking its fresh cut, while missing or undecodable `gc/state` adopts reconstructed authority only, performs zero catalog deletion, and leaves drain work to the next invocation.

`CaRefPreFoldDrainCore` is the sole owner of adopted-parent validation, catalog drain, conclusive CAS resolution, and fresh-cut ordering, and exports an immutable full-catalog token/value pair to the ref-plan consumer boundary.
The pre-fold witness requires an actual token-advancing exact `Removing` deletion and verifies the drained row is absent from both the consumed cut and the plan.
On a sibling upload failure, successful sibling bodies remain ordinary GC-reclaimable debris while the poisoned sibling is never uploaded; result merging does not occur after failure.

An unmatched adopted-parent opaque life remains observable but is excluded from the successor seal and does not suppress pool-wide destructive cleanup; a valid manifest candidate can be physically deleted in the same round.

Every acquired ordinary GC invocation, including `DEFER`, runs exactly one independently paced `cas/ns/` janitor page and one later catalog cut while the hot immutable `RefPlan` still uses exactly one `cas/ns/stream/` LIST plus one later catalog cut.

`Gc::runNamespaceJanitorPage` owns the bounded page, post-page catalog cut, exact GC-fence check, warnings, and `namespace_cleanup` metrics, and never performs a catalog lifecycle transition or contributes to the hot walk plan.
The folding path passes its `FoldResult::suppress_destructive` verdict to the janitor helper, while `DEFER` calls the same helper with deletion suppressed because it has no complete fold verdict.

A janitor page advances its cursor only when its catalog cut is unambiguous, deletion is globally admitted, and no candidate observes fence loss; suppressed, ambiguous, or fence-lost pages retain the old cursor for authoritative retry.
Malformed keys, `NotFound`, and exact-token mismatch are decided per key and may advance the janitor page, while corrupt or backend-rejected cursor reset behavior remains exact-token based.

Suppression, catalog ambiguity, and fence loss each retain the selected janitor page; fence loss stops subsequent deletes without rolling back earlier exact deletes, and a final fence recheck prevents progress after a retained-only page or authority loss following the last delete.

The namespace janitor retains current `Creating`, `Live`, and `Removing` life identifiers through the catalog reverse index; an absent identifier is a deletion candidate, duplicate current identifiers suppress the whole page, and malformed keys are reported and skipped.

Corrupt or oversized janitor progress performs no LIST or delete and is reset only against its exact token; a backend-rejected cursor is likewise reset exactly before the error is surfaced, while cursor CAS conflicts are ignored.
A fresh `NamespaceJanitor` resumes a durable partial cursor and resets it at end-of-tree; LIST omissions defer work to a later cycle rather than coupling lifecycle progress to physical visibility.
The current GC phase named `namespace_cleanup` is a perpetual janitor phase and is not retired marker residue.
Parsed listed keys can nominate malformed or foreign stream objects for diagnostics or leak cleanup, but they can never install table state.
`Gc::rebuildBaseline` must pass the immutable catalog cut and exact checkpoint, and a catalog-named life without usable frontier authority is retain/refuse rather than destructive.

`CasOrphanManifestSweep::activeManifestKeys` must use exact-frontier recovery for owner protection and exact replay through `committed_through`; until that authority is available, catalog-named namespaces are retain-only.
`planRefCleanup` documents snapshot, durable-cursor, and optional-checkpoint boundaries and does not describe cleanup items or a durable `Removed` snapshot.
At the unmatched `parent_ref_lives` branch, `buildRefWalkPlan` increments `CasGcUnmatchedAdoptedParentLives`, logs the exact `NamespaceLifePhysicalId`, drops the aggregate row, and emits no plan row.
[C1] requires `loop()` and `heartbeatLoop()` to check `isVanished()` at each wake and self-exit, preventing new GC rounds after `Vanished`.
The modeled `GcStoppedAfterForget` invariant holds even on idempotent FORGET and post-FORGET `GC START`, because the Admin gate refuses GC on a non-`Live` pool.

During Stage-A destruction suppression, the janitor withholds `deleteExact`; its `namespace_cleanup` metrics record seen keys and a `suppressed` count, so six rounds with zero deletions do not prove permanent orphaning.
`Context` provides `getContentAddressedGarbageCollectionLog` and `getContentAddressedLog` getters for CAS system-log wiring.

The `SYSTEM` query surface includes `CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GARBAGE_COLLECTION`, `CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GC_REBUILD`, and `CONTENT_ADDRESSED_DROP_POOL_MEMBER`, with access checks and `runContentAddressed*` helpers.
`Interpreters/SystemLog.h` registers the `ContentAddressedGarbageCollectionLog` and `ContentAddressedLog` system logs.

The parser and AST support `CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GARBAGE_COLLECTION`, `CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GC_REBUILD`, and `CONTENT_ADDRESSED_DROP_POOL_MEMBER`, including the `content_addressed_gc_rebuild_force` field and round-trip parser coverage.
The `magic_enum::enum_range` for `ASTSystemQuery::Type` must be widened to `[0,255]` because the added CAS `SYSTEM` query types exceed the default range.

A build heartbeat is durable in the pool before the first blob PUT via the pool-wide gc/hb pulse plus the writer's mount object build-watermark floor; there is no separate builds/<build_id> object in the current layout.
Regular GC deletion outcomes are classified as deleted | absent | replaced (412 = resurrection won) | spared, and retire entries are dropped only on confirmed outcomes.

The force-Read override HEADs only fire from `closeBlob` on hashes touched in the current fold window (`cur_edges == 0`); `settleRetiredBelow`'s quiescent-entry path never issues a HEAD and must not be changed to do so.
On a resurrect supersede the fold keeps exactly one retired entry per hash: the stale entry is dropped, not kept alongside the fresh re-condemn, and the retired list stays hash-sorted.

Sharded-GC correctness was validated by S15: identical oracle checksums and `dangling=0` under both `gc_shards=1` (default) and `gc_shards=2`, with reducer memory flat (0.60->0.61 GB) and orphan backlog fully drained in both configurations.

Under `suppress_destructive`, both the `manifest_deletes` phase and the orphan sweep are gated closed: `mf_cleanup_now` is an empty map, and the orphan-sweep delete loop consumes `folded.orphan_sweep.nominations`, which is empty because `planManifestCursorPage` is only invoked when `!suppress_destructive`.

The frontier round's "universe" is exactly every `Live`/`Removing` row of the round's own frozen catalog cut and nothing else; an older comment defining it as "hint ∪ sealed cursors ∪ catalog Live/Removing entries" is stale and contradicts the code, which implements only the catalog-cut definition.

GC's raw baseline rebuild condemns nothing: it only rebuilds cursors and edges. An earlier version ended the pass by LISTing `blobs/` and condemning every physically-present body outside the rebuilt edge set, but this was found unsafe (r5-finding-4) because both legs of the traversal (owner replay and the trimmed-but-live manifest pass) are listing-driven, so a store that omits a durable key from one enumeration hides a live owner while the same pass condemns the blob that owner pins — an observed real failure mode (the `0x1430c` shape), not a hypothetical.

Patch parts / lightweight deletes are first-class GC reachability roots: a patch manifest references the base part's patched data columns plus its own delta blobs, and while a patch ref is active it transitively keeps alive both its own delta blobs and the base blobs it references, even if the base part is otherwise superseded, provided the MARK walk treats patch manifests as roots. When a patch is materialized into the base via merge, the patch ref is released and its uniquely-owned delta blobs become sweepable. Patch-on-content-addressed-base is flagged as not yet fully model-checked in the v3 design's residual-risk list.

A stateless/ref-less reader that attaches by reading the catalog and registers no `/parts` ref is invisible to the per-process `use_count()==1` MARK-union fence, which is a valid cross-node fence only for replicas holding a `/parts` ref; owning replicas can release refs after `old_parts_lifetime` (480s) mid-SELECT, sweeping the manifest/blobs out from under the read. The preferred fix is an ephemeral reader pin (a Keeper node or equivalent) created at query start naming the parts/snapshot read, auto-released on session end/crash; this is distinct from the lost-replica timeout, which is a genuine leak needing a separate long-dead-replica reaping rule.

`CaGcAckFloorCore.tla`'s `SabotageClampNoSuppress` config, which removes the `~clampedL` graduation guard, reproduces the 2026-07-03 night incident of 31 dangling blobs as an `INV_NO_DANGLE` counterexample; the shipped clamp-suppression guard (`suppress_destructive` gating `Gc::graduationDue`, `CasGc.cpp:1360`) blocks graduation and pending deletes while any shard is clamped, so held refs persist in `landed` until a later clamp-free pass consumes them.

`putDeterministicArtifact` is the write-once helper for GC objects whose bytes are a pure function of their inputs (source-edge runs, fold seals): a `putIfAbsent` precondition failure is resolved by reading the existing object back and comparing bytes — byte-equal means the writer's own replay landed and is adopted as a no-op, while divergent bytes throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` as an impossible case. It is deliberately not used for observation-bearing artifacts like GC outcome logs, which use first-durable-write-wins byte-adopt semantics instead, and never for blob bodies because the fresh-tag rule makes two attempts of the same logical create legitimately differ.

In GC sharding, a shard with an empty delta bucket and no condemned entries in the parent summary copies the parent's run references verbatim ("pure carry", zero run I/O); a missing parent summary entry on a non-fresh pool is `CORRUPTED_DATA`, never silently treated as zero.

Generation pruning (GC phase 13) keeps the last `gc_snap_generations_to_keep` generations (default 3; 0 keeps everything for forensics) and deletes wholesale by LIST-and-delete-everything under the generation prefix, bounded to 64 generations per round. A generation still referenced by the live seal is skipped but the cursor still advances past it regardless, so leak-freedom depends entirely on the post-CAS hand-off reclaim in phase 14.

Namespace removal has no physical-empty handshake: the writer changes the catalog row from `Live` to `Removing`, appends the exact ref removals plus a `RemoveNamespace` op, and deletes nothing itself. GC's fold attaches cleanup evidence to that opaque life row, and only a later GC invocation's pre-fold drain exact-CAS-deletes the matching `Removing` catalog row before any successor plan can be published; the perpetual namespace janitor and orphan-manifest sweep reclaim the physical debris independently, and a same-name birth waits only for the catalog row to disappear.

Attribution of the night's 11 concurrent GC clamps was: RustFS returned false 404s on HEAD during a metacache storm caused by the `rustfs#3231` overwrite-leak's directory bloat (00:37-00:55); the clamps rose with the storm and self-released when it subsided (~01:01), and the bodies the false 404s claimed were missing had never actually been deleted (no `tree_delete` for the pinned manifests). The full causal chain is: leak -> directory bloat -> metacache storm -> false 404s on HEAD -> GC clamps -> (pre-fix) graduation proceeding over unfolded landed events -> dangling blobs.

CAS probe A (the ref-scan disagreement detector) reports each hole with the ref-log id and its direction: holes missing from the fold's own (second) scan are explainable by concurrent deletion, but holes missing from the pre-fold (first) scan are not — the object existed at the second walk and its id sits below what the first walk had already observed, so the first walk should have returned it.

The Stage B strategic-review concentration proposal's replacement namespace-removal sequence is: (1) catalog transitions Live to Removing; (2) the fenced owner appends the terminal record; (3) GC folds the terminal record and performs one bounded cleanup pass; (4) GC writes a stable retirement marker derived only from RootNamespace; (5) GC durably publishes a fold seal with that namespace's cursor pruned; (6) GC exact-deletes `_ckpt`; (7) catalog entry deletion happens last.

Ordering the retirement marker before `_ckpt` deletion means even catalog loss cannot turn a namespace-removal window into a fresh birth; creation must check both the retirement marker and the namespace's `_ckpt` by exact key before admission and refuse if either exists; a listing omission can leak old objects but cannot make a retired namespace visible again because it is never re-admitted.

Even under the no-namespace-reuse simplification, catalog authority, the `Creating` publication exclusion, the `Removing` positive-ownership exclusion, the exact-next frontier probe, durable holds, and the delete-site in-degree re-read must not be cut, because they prevent data loss independently of rebirth; a temporary "refuse while old objects survive, retry after GC" rule does not substitute for them since LIST cannot certify old-object absence.

C2's widening past its three originally-named sites is justified because `marker_key` is the guard that the physical manifest and verbatim passes consult, so they cannot run without a resolved life; the still-sentinel-keyed `namespaceFilesPrefix` is correct because every writer of namespace files is also sentinel-keyed, making that layer Task 6's responsibility rather than a C2 leftover.

The GC round's exact durable key layout: `gc/state` (controller state, one per pool, strict fail-closed CAGT-magic proto), `gc/hb` (advisory heartbeat, fixed 24-byte binary), `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/fold_seal` (write-once fold seal), `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/.../<round>/<shard>` (retire outcome log), `cas/refs/<ns>/_log/<txn_id>` (ref log txn), `cas/refs/<ns>/_snap/<id>.proto` (ref snapshot).

Blob reachability is source-edge set membership, not a counter: one source edge is (BlobRef, source_id) where source_id = CityHash128(namespace + ref + path), with 0 reserved as the sentinel key for kCondemned rows. The edge set is idempotent under re-fold, so retries and competing attempts produce byte-identical runs.

"Spared" means a condemned blob's in-degree recovered because a publish re-referenced it; the retired entry is dropped and recovery wins even past the graduation floor. "Forgotten" has no live meaning in this subsystem — the memory-noted GForget/GcSnap::forget design is superseded by pruneSupersededGenerations (wholesale generation retention).

There is no crash-resume step in the GC round: the whole round commits in the single `gc/state` CAS at the end, so a crashed pass leaves only attempt-scoped debris under its own unadopted lease.seq, never adopted and later reclaimed by `pruneSupersededGenerations` or the Task-7 hand-off. Every pre-CAS destructive action is justified by previously-published durable state (`delete_pending`), making replay under a fresh attempt idempotent.

The orphan-manifest sweep gates deletion by `prefixEligible`, a durable watermark-only fact (`min_active > build_sequence`, or the retired sentinel `min_active==UINT64_MAX`, or an older epoch; a missing watermark means NOT eligible), and skips any key still in `activeManifestKeys(ns)` (committed + live precommits + manifests removed above the durable fold cursor). It never GETs a condemned body to revive it.

Stage B Task 5's restated invariant: no same-name namespace entry can be created while any GC-held state (cursor, cleanup item, seal row) for the previous life survives; under this ordering, the catalog entry for a dropped table survives until the terminal record folds (a GC-round latency), so `CREATE TABLE` of a just-dropped name is refused — today as a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Pool/CasRefCatalog.cpp:236`) — until the next fold, which will burn stateless CI lanes that drop-and-recreate names constantly.

Capture-at-deposition (recording `NamespaceLifeId` at fold time rather than re-deriving it from the catalog) is mandatory because the stale-leader TLA+ sabotage shows that re-deriving the incarnation after rebirth targets the new life directly, causing data loss.
A removed namespace whose only residue is `_files` promotes its cleanup item to `Completed` on the first fold, so the janitor cannot key its reclaim logic off `Pending` state alone.

Non-per-namespace fold-seal capacity terms (`btr` per run segment, `cnd` per gc-shard) are untouched by the removal-ordering decision and do not disappear along with the Σ-index-set capacity argument.

Probe A detects CAS ref-prefix LIST incompleteness via two independent enumerations per GC round (the pre-fold defer scan and fold's own enumeration); it compares per-namespace id sets and reports a hole only when the id is below the OTHER enumeration's own maximum for that namespace, which excludes ordinary in-flight appends between the two walks.

Probe A has two documented blind spots it does not catch: a hole that reproduces identically in both enumerations, and a namespace dropped wholesale from one enumeration (no `ref_tables` entry, so the comparison loop never visits it); widening the witness rule to use the pre-scan's own maximum was considered and rejected because it would permanently block the cursor on a namespace whose logs were legitimately cleaned between the walks.

`stale_edge_verdict` returns `unchecked` on any partial scan, with positive findings still checked first, because a partial scan can only weaken a proof of absence, never invalidate evidence of presence.

The chosen fix (Fix 4) for the deposed-leader stray-Clean defect makes GC freshness metadata add-only: GC never transitions Condemned to Clean on a spare (the spare-side `clearSparedMeta` call and helper are removed); only a writer that has displaced the body with a fresh incarnation token publishes Clean, via `uploadFromSource` + `writeResurrectMetaClean`/`copyForwardFromCondemned`. Accepted cost: a spared hash stays Condemned until a writer resurrects it (write amplification on recurring-hash churn); normal reads never consult the meta so this is safe.
The hot/cold layout split changed GC discovery to GET gc/state + LIST cas/refs/, making discovery proportional to ref shards rather than manifest backlog.
GC runs as a background lease-holder loop and its safety does not depend on leadership uniqueness; concurrent or stale leaders may duplicate work but must not mis-delete.
The advisory GC heartbeat is stored in `gc/hb` as `{owner, hb_seq}` and is advanced independently of round progress to prevent a live slow leader from being falsely stolen.
A forced GC rebuild over-protects unowned manifests that are not provably build-dead, preferring bounded leaks over violating `INV_OVER_COUNT_ONLY` through under-counting.
GC safety is independent of the advisory heartbeat; the heartbeat is the minimal addition needed to prevent a slow leader's frozen round sequence from triggering a false steal.

The root-local model shows that a target-sharded fold needs one global coordinator fence and paired old-binding `−1` deltas; per-reducer fencing or inferring the old target from the new ref is unsafe.
The E3 GC redesign used root-local part manifests and source edges identified by `(ManifestId, path)`, removed the registry, and added a shard-incarnation ABA guard.

The E4 GC and writer settlement uses a one-pass heartbeat ack-floor round, writer point-reads of freshness metadata instead of a `RetireView`, retired rows inside the snapshot run, and a ref snapshot plus append log instead of a mutable root-shard manifest.
Retired rows are represented as `kCondemned` sentinel rows inside the snapshot run rather than as a separate retired-list object.
The GC-side ack-floor one-pass round is current, while the writer-side ack-floor and `RetireView` synchronization was deleted by `55b76af5998`; these are separate mechanisms.
The regular GC round is one pass consisting of a heartbeat ack floor, one `LIST` discovery sweep, a three-cursor fold, pre-CAS deletes, and one `gc/state` CAS.

The GC lease is work de-duplication rather than mutual exclusion: one `gc/state` CAS adopts a round, attempt-scoped artifacts isolate leaders, pre-CAS destructive work uses published state, and exact-token deletes protect newer incarnations.
The D1 implementation plan replaces `gc/registry` discovery with `LIST(cas/refs/)` and reclaims empty ref-shard objects so `dropNamespace` no longer leaks a monotone registry and empty shard objects.

The D1 design collapses the prior fence coordinates into two orthogonal coordinates: immutable shard `incarnation` for identity and birth ordering, plus pool-global GC `round` for the writer retire-view floor.

D1 makes `LIST(cas/refs/)` the discovery authority, retains ambiguity detection across pages as a fail-closed condition, and removes `gc/registry`, `RootsRegistry`, `rootsRegistryKey`, `ensureRegistered`, the registry-fence sub-step, and the `_registry` cursor branch.

`dropNamespace` appends an explicit tombstone as the last journal event after ref removals, and GC deletes the shard only when it is empty, tombstoned, and folded past a completed fence using `deleteExact(rootShardKey(ns, shard), token)`.
After registry removal, GC fences only discovered shards from `LIST(cas/refs/)`; an absent shard is not minted or fenced, and create ordering is supplied by the precommit gate.

The consolidation target explicitly assigns GC protocol documentation to cover lease/election, rounds, orphan and ref removal, shard reclaim, incarnation, registry removal, attempt-scoped generations, TLA+ references, and S3 budget links.
The ack-floor GC redesign replaces O(universe) per-round fence and recheck phases with a merged per-server heartbeat, a current retired list, and a one-pass three-cursor merge.

The current retired-list design adds `RetiredEntry::condemn_round`, adds `GcState::retired_refs`, uses `cas_gc_state` version 4, rejects v3 fail-closed, and has `RetireView::refresh` GET `gc/state` followed by each referenced retired-list object without LIST.

The planned one-pass ack-floor round computes the heartbeat floor before discovery, folds and merges deltas, deletes graduated entries by exact token, writes retired-list objects, and then performs one `gc/state` CAS; `fence` and `recheck` are removed.
The redesigned regular GC round targets O(delta) plus O(servers) S3 requests; its only universe-proportional operation is the existing LIST sweep, which costs O(universe/1000) LIST requests.

The retired list is one current sorted candidate set referenced by `gc/state.retired_refs`; per-round retired sets keyed by `retiredKey(...)` and the multi-round `RetireView` fetch protocol are removed.

`gc/state` removes `fence_version`, adds current retired-list references and checksums, and is updated with one CAS per pass containing the round, generation adoption, retired references, and coverage.
`fence_round` is no longer bumped every round; it remains only as the birth floor stamped at root-shard creation for THM-NO-RETURN newborn ordering.
Graduation is two-phase: a pass marks fresh graduates with `delete_pending = true` and keeps them published, while `deleteExact` runs only for entries already pending in the previous published list.
Snapshot-run streaming scope includes T2 streaming reads and T0 reference-parent runs for empty-delta shards; T1 delta-runs are deferred to a subsequent specification.

Implemented retention skips at generation granularity and advances `snap_pruned_through` over every visited generation; when a reference moves off a skipped generation, hand-off deletes the whole `gc/gen/<g>/` prefix rather than one run, preventing leaks of the rest of that generation's artifacts.

The rebuild plan uses attempt iteration over batches of at most `rebuild_edge_budget` edges, feeding the previous attempt's runs back as `prior_runs`; this provides O(budget) memory without new spill/merge classes.
GC trim uses `mutateShard` as a `WholeShard` queue item, so trim rewrites no longer race writers even though trim still flushes alone.

If any fold pass records a clamp anomaly, destruction is suppressed: no graduations or redeletes occur, pending entries carry `UNCHANGED`, condemn/spare continue, and deletes resume on the first clamp-free pass; the pass emits a warning and increments `CasGcClampSuppressedPasses`.
GC Lever A skips the expensive in-degree snapshot rebuild on rounds with no destructive decision; Lever B, an incremental point-updatable in-degree store, remains out of scope.

The DEFER decision is true exactly when changed-shard count is below `fold_threshold`, no destructive decision is due, and `rounds_since_last_fold` is below `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds`; otherwise the round FOLDs.
Using a stale heartbeat acknowledgement for a renewal is conservative for the GC floor because it can only lower `min_ack` and delay graduation; lease expiry is the failure that must be avoided.

The phase-4 GC optimization skips unchanged namespaces so an idle round approaches O(servers) reads and a small-delta round costs O(delta), with a mandatory TLA+ proof that owner-removal events are never skipped.

The dangling-precommit fix uses a fold-side, watermark-keyed force-Read: `ShardCoverage` records the minimal live precommit binding, and `computeDiscoverDecisions` overrides `Skip` when that precommit is provably dead.

The resurrect-reupload fix keys blob condemnation on `(hash, current token)` instead of only on the hash, and re-condemns a current token when a touched hash has net in-degree zero and a prior retired token differs.
Build::abandon retires build_seq after its precommit-removal CAS, while alive is set false early.
Graduation is re-keyed from condemn_round < min_ack to condemn_round < current_round, with min_ack removed from the GC fold interface.
After v3, the retired list is GC-private: writers make condemned decisions through per-hash `.meta` point reads and do not read `RetiredSet`.

Retired-in-snapshot preserves settlement semantics including condemn, carry, round-paced graduation, `delete_pending`, redelete, clamp suppression, the pre-CAS single delete site, resurrect-supersede, `.meta` writes, B170 events, and GC-log counters.

The two-cursor merge settles a pending row by exact-token redelete at d = 0, spares any row at d > 0, graduates a nonpending row when `condemn_round < current_round`, and otherwise carries it unchanged.
In-place journal trimming was replaced by cleanup of `_log` and superseded `_snap` objects only when both durable cursor coverage and observed snapshot coverage exist.
CAS listing and exact-delete handling is intended to share a callback-based `forEachListedKey` iterator and a `classifyDeleteOutcome` classifier across GC, fsck, and orphan-manifest cleanup.

`GcState::fence_seq` is write-only vestigial state because GC outcome and retire keys use `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)`; its proto field is removed and field number 3/name `fence_seq` are reserved.
`ShardCoverage::folded_cursor` and `ShardCoverage::incarnation` have no production readers and are removed from the fold-seal format while the `ShardIncarnation` type itself is retained.

GC fold body reads should size each fresh `ReadBufferFromS3` from the known listed/meta body size plus small slack, capped at the current default; the expected effect is approximately 99% less fold-buffer churn with no behavior change.

Manifest debris must be drained before deleting the victim mount slot because deleting the mount body removes `floorForNamespace` watermark authority and would make the debris ineligible forever; the decommission command is the epoch authority and can sweep old-epoch prefixes.
The rev.6 GC-defense audit treats zero S3 requests spent fighting a foreign writer on hot paths as the compliance principle; incidental checks and CAS-linearized commits are compliant by definition.
A new GC leader starts lease observation afresh, delaying fencing by one round without weakening safety because fencing is a liveness and cleanup mechanism.
The rev.6 GC-defense audit keeps the `gc/state` CAS, orphan-sweep prior-epoch gate, and fold-lag machinery because they are GC or intra-node mechanisms rather than foreign-writer defenses.
The recommended root-cause fix for the fetch-by-relink residual is a liveness re-check at the GC pre-CAS `deleteExact` site rather than restoring blanket promote-time HEAD and `loadMeta` probes.
Reader retention is implemented as incremental removal deferral rather than refolding the entire pinned closure each GC round.
Fetch-by-relink handoff pins and reader snapshot pins share only the GC retention-overlay primitive and are independently shippable features.
Any future §5 revival must keep spare tombstones uncleared until a writer resurrects the blob with a fresh token.

CAS runs use sorted NDJSON with no blocks, footer, or `seek`; `RunFileReader::seek`, `inDegreeInGeneration`, and `SourceEdgeKeyCodec::seekPrefix` are deleted because production consumers read runs sequentially, accepting approximately twice the bytes with re-binarizing `cas_run` as the localized fallback.
`cas_gc_outcomes` is not deterministic: it uses idempotent `putIfAbsent`, and replay adopts an existing durable object after decoding rather than treating byte inequality as a correctness failure.
Only `RunKind::SourceEdge` is live for standalone `cas_run`; `BlobDelta` and `TargetShardDelta` are dead, while `ManifestEntries` remains only for the embedded part-manifest stream.
The production fold uses a hand-written two-cursor merge of the prior run stream and scattered deltas; no k-way line-based merger is introduced.

The chosen interim response to the LIST-hole hypothesis was mechanism-agnostic detection: compare two ref-prefix enumerations before advancing a cursor and compare intended-to-fold records with actually applied records; the permanent journal-chain fix remains required before release.
GC read parallelism is safe because tables fold independently and log reads can be prefetched while prior logs are applied; the ordering constraint applies to folding, not fetching.

The concurrent-leader GC fix stores every per-round artifact, including `retired` and `outcomes`, under `gc/gen/<gen>/attempt/<a>/...`, where `<a>` is the folding leader's lease sequence; a lease-guarded adopt CAS publishes `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)`, and readers resolve only that adopted pair.

The root-local part-manifest design retired the `listedTok` token-diff discovery skip: a LIST match may not authorize skipping a manifest or owner-transition fold read.

Catalog deletion does not require physical emptiness: `_ckpt`, stream, `_snap`, and `_files` residue may remain for the perpetual janitor or a family-specific sweep.
The ref-delta intake has no quiet or expected-next 404 frontier: every catalog target must resolve through its exact CTE.
Under the amended v9 intake, `LIST` is a zero-trust hint; fold progress advances arithmetically and destructive work requires a per-namespace frontier proof.

Catalog admission must reject creation unless the encoded catalog plus worst-case fold cursor and removal reservations fit within both the catalog cap and the 256 MiB fold-seal cap.

Orphan-manifest nomination must exact-GET and decode M, submit neutral current-count touches without B2 or unmatched-removal accounting, adopt them through the fold seal/gc/state CAS, and exact-delete M only afterward.

Catalog admission must enforce the additive reservation predicate fold_fixed + Σ reserve_cursor(entry) + Σ reserve_removing_cleanup(entry) + Σ reserve_hold(entry) <= fold_seal_cap in addition to encoded_catalog(post).size <= catalog_cap.

Classification-4 wire fields require exact bounded names and values, duplicate-field rejection, and a byte-exact worst-case reservation including escaped namespace text, framing, newline, and trailer growth.
Arithmetic exact-key intake is the intended mechanism for closing LIST omissions; the former Probe A seam was deleted rather than retained as a sampled store-quality detector.
Parallel GC fetching should be bounded by the number of in-flight manifest bodies and should leave application strictly ordered while fetching log and manifest bodies ahead of use.
A proposed manifest cache is keyed by `ManifestId`, scoped to one fold round, bounded in bytes, and dropped at round end; avoiding one redundant edge avoids both its HEAD and GET trips.

Blob in-degree is derived from a folded set of source-edge deltas keyed by `(kind, hash, source_manifest)` rather than stored as a mutable counter; set semantics can delay reclamation but cannot accelerate deletion.

The ack-floor GC round replaces fence and recheck phases with a three-cursor streaming merge and one `gc/state` CAS; graduation requires `condemn_round < min_ack` and two-phase `delete_pending` handling.
All decision-bearing GC artifacts, including `retired` and `outcomes`, are under `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/`, and only the adopted attempt is reader-visible.

The useful manifest-body cache scope is one GC round: an op-scoped or transaction-scoped cache saves nothing, while a round-scoped cache can avoid cross-transaction re-reads; the HEAD-before-GET pair remains vetoed from change.
GC, orphan sweep, and fsck should share a structured deletion outcome vocabulary: deleted, missing, token mismatch, unsupported, and failed.

Retired entries can ride the source-edge snapshot as condemned-sentinel rows, reducing the GC merge from three cursors to two; a separate incremental LSM snapshot is an independent later optimization.
GC streams the three-cursor merge but accumulates the round's `std::vector<BlobDelta>` in memory, so a large mass-drop delta can cause an OOM and repeated lack of progress for that shard.

The later GCR-1 re-triage concluded that `rebuildBaseline` computes the mount-lease ack-floor and installs `gc/state` with a fail-closed CAS, so floor-gated graduation protects post-snapshot writer objects without refusing rebuild while writers are mounted.
The P3-B1 fix invokes an `on_lease_acquired` hook immediately after `acquireOrRenewLease`, sets `i_am_leader`, and pulses the heartbeat before folding begins.

sweepManifestCursorPage is test-only code: it was moved to src/Disks/tests/cas_sweep_test_support.h as sweepManifestCursorPageForTest, and no production translation unit calls it because exact-token deletion without source-edge retirement or gc/state adoption would recreate the accounting hole.
T5 removes `Gc::sampleRefListQuality` and its `ref_list_probe` call, so a regular GC round no longer performs a second full ref-prefix LIST for store-quality sampling.
`UniversePolicy::kDefault` is `Authoritative`; the destructive gate requires an authoritative universe, `frontier_namespaces > 0`, and `frontier_proven == frontier_namespaces`.

After the destruction flip, the dropped-pool-member integration test expects janitor residue to drain to `janitor_pending == 0`, while checking `lifeless_keys=0` on every poll and retaining final `dangling=0` and `unaccounted=0` checks.
`cas_gc_maintenance_state` has no janitor invocation, `GcState`, fold, catalog, DEFER, or round-publication coupling.
Lifecycle physical cleanup is not part of the pre-fold drain: `suppress_destructive` does not govern it, and the perpetual `cas/ns/` janitor plus orphan-manifest sweep own physical debris.
No janitor state is stored in `gc/state` or a fold seal, and there is no lifecycle-specific cleanup attempt.
GC must not advance a cursor over records whose enumeration completeness it cannot prove from authoritative data rather than assuming a listing is complete.
The in-degree reducer is intentionally not changed: a set cannot cancel an element it never received, and materializing an unmatched negative edge would create false deletion.

The eager-unlink helper `isEagerContentAddressedUnlink` and six per-method `remove*` eager branches are replaced by subclass dispatch, with durable deletion represented as a staged intent materialized at commit.

The current GC implementation (Gc class, CasGc.h) is a leader-paced ack-floor redesign (spec 2026-07-02): one pass per round consisting of a heartbeat ack floor over MountLease.observed_gc_round, a three-cursor merge fold, two-phase condemn/graduation deletion, and a single gc/state CAS; the older fence_round/recheck terminology survives only as fossil comments/variable names.

Task A7 serializes the manual `SYSTEM ... GC` round against the background GC loop using a dedicated gc_round_mutex rather than the scheduler's existing `mutex`, because loop() deliberately releases `mutex` before running a round so that stop() and heartbeatLoop() are not blocked; holding `mutex` across a long fold would freeze the GC heartbeat and stall shutdown.

GC baseline rebuild is deliberately over-protective rather than under-protective: a build alive across journal trim has no journal evidence, so its manifests look unowned; the rebuild includes edges for every unowned manifest that is not provably build-dead, over-protecting rather than risking under-count. An unowned manifest that later dies with no journal evidence leaks its blob's edges for one bounded rebuild-to-rebuild window, `fsck`-visible as `unaccounted` — preferred to violating `INV_OVER_COUNT_ONLY`.

A destructive GC gate based only on `proven == total` accepts an empty universe vacuously because `0 == 0`; the fix adds an explicit nonempty-authority predicate so the gate cannot be satisfied by having nothing to prove.

`cas-gc-rebuild`'s security verdict: it cannot delete live data directly (deletions still flow through the normal round's ack-floor plus two-phase plus exact-token path), and a crafted owner state that makes rebuild under-count requires full owner-plane write access, which already implies total pool compromise (SEC-3) — the trimmed-history guard closes the naive truncation path. Residual risks: FORCE only skips the healthy-pool check (operational risk, not a safety bypass); rebuild does a full-universe discover-and-fold (O(all shards + all journals)), an expensive pool-wide sweep an attacker with SYSTEM access could trigger repeatedly (shares the SEC-4 decode/fold exhaustion surface); and a concurrent GC leader's round CAS and rebuild's `gc/state` install can contend, so rebuild must be verified to respect GC leadership or a split-baseline is possible.

D7: the SQL `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` verb and the offline `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild` command are NOT duplication — both call the same `Gc::rebuildBaseline` core through two deliberately inverse-gated surfaces (live/writable vs offline/read-only), and this dual surface should be kept as-is.

There are two independent sharding axes in GC that are deliberately different and easy to confuse: `blobShard` (blob-hash high64 % gc_shards, for in-degree work) versus `Store::shardOf` (CityHash64(ref_name) % root_shards, for the owner journal). There are also two independent lease/watermark concepts: the GC lease inside `gc/state`, versus the mount lease / build watermark at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount`; `computeHeartbeatFloor` fences only the latter, never the GC lease.

The RemovalReady state costs less wire-format surface than a life-keyed-cursor alternative: cursor identity appears in eight files spanning the wire grammar, every builder/parser, REBUILD, fsck, and the sweep's coverage lookup, versus one enum value, one codec branch, one transition, and the five predicate sites for RemovalReady. Life-keyed cursors also create a new corner case (a reborn name's fresh-life cursor coexists with a dead-life cursor nothing prunes), so they only relocate the retirement-tracking problem rather than avoiding it.

The Stage B strategic review's invariant rulings: weaken byte-exact fold-seal capacity reservation to a generous over-covering bound (count times a conservative constant, hard namespace cap ~10^4) instead of exact worst-case arithmetic; cut the `Creating`-forbids-publication write-path check as a separate production-path obligation since `resolveNamespaceLife` already loops until `Live` and is the sole life source; cut incarnation-scoped fold cursor re-keying once prune-before-entry-delete is the pinned invariant; weaken the `_ckpt` conflict-is-corruption join to a semantic-max merge (corruption only on genuinely incomparable fields).

Under strict removal ordering, the worst cases "two cleanup rows for one namespace" and "a cleanup row with no catalog entry" become unconstructible (both require rebirth before the first removal retired); the worst-case capacity test should be replaced by an anomaly check that fires if GC ever observes an entry-less cleanup row.

Probe A is reported-not-gated: a soak can go GREEN with confirmed enumeration holes (`nonzero_in=28/88 reads`) because folding aborts and nothing is deleted, which is defensible while the product fails closed, but is flagged as a decision that should be made deliberate now that the holes are confirmed rather than suspected.

The ack-floor GC redesign drops `process_epoch` as a separate merged-heartbeat field because the writable path already sets `process_epoch = writer_epoch` (`CasStore.cpp:157`) and the sweep consumes `writer_epoch` unchanged, so a distinct field would be redundant.

The ack-floor design renamed the sabotage control `SabotageDeleteAtFloor` to `SabotageIgnoreAckFloor` because an `r < min_ack` vs `r ≤ min_ack` off-by-one is provably still safe under the publish-order invariant, so the load-bearing control is "ignores the floor entirely", not the exact boundary.

An optional pre-pass refresh for the promote copy-forward tokenless-blob race fix (spec §3) was deliberately deferred rather than implemented: it is a fast-path-only optimization, not required for correctness, so it was left unscheduled rather than turned into a task.
Per-round LIST hunting for deposed-leader GC debris had already been removed; stale generations are now reclaimed by ordinary retention pruning with zero extra hot-path requests.
The three observed ref-log keys were deleted at 16:53:59 after folding aborted and a later complete enumeration reclaimed them; this occurrence produced no leak.

Before the redesign, 100,000 tables with 8 root shards each required approximately 800,000 CAS-PUTs and 1,600,000 GETs per GC round because the fence and recheck traversed the entire root-shard universe.

The redesigned steady-state round budget is one LIST sweep plus O(servers) heartbeat GETs, O(D) changed-shard GETs, O(window) manifest GETs, O(gc_shards) run GET/PUTs, candidate HEADs, graduated DELETEs, O(D) coverage PUTs, and one `gc/state` CAS, with no O(universe) GET/PUT phase.

Before T2, a snapshot run was materialized three times—by `CasObjectStorageBackend::get`, `RunFileReader::full`, and `readPriorEdges`—for peak memory of approximately 3 × O(active edges) per GC shard; the target example estimated about 24 GB RAM for one fold.

Before T0, every pass rewrote every GC-shard snapshot run even for an empty delta, causing an idle pool to pay two snapshot sizes per round; at the target scale and 5-minute rounds this was estimated as terabytes per day of churn.
Opening a snapshot run in streaming mode uses a HEAD, a ranged tail GET for the footer, and a body `getStream`; resident run memory is O(block) while the wire bytes are unchanged.
With T0, an idle round that has no changes touches zero snapshot-run objects and consists of the LIST sweep, heartbeats, and one `gc/state` CAS.
Idle GC over a static 20M-row, 400-part pool used about 1,362 `CasGcGet`, 643 `CasBlobHead`, and 457 `CasRootGet` operations per round, roughly 2,500 S3 operations per round despite no changes.

The observed GC round duration grew from 87 ms at 400 parts to 92.6 seconds at 10,000 tables and 398 seconds at 100,000 parts, demonstrating O(ref-universe/object-count) scaling; fsck also becomes O(objects) and timed out at 100,000 parts.
Partitioned inserts in S11 require O(partitions) CAS commits, taking about 10 seconds for a 256-partition insert; deferred GC during 64 delete rounds allowed orphaned parts to outpace disk capacity.

`Gc::fold` performs a streaming two-cursor merge over the entire prior generation's source-edge run, reading the whole prior generation and writing a whole new consolidated run even when one edge or no edge changed.
The resurrect-replaced repair adds one HEAD only for a touched condemned transition; quiescent graduation through `settleRetiredBelow` takes no additional HEAD.
The codecs-v3 phase-3 soak completed with `dangling=0`, equal oracle counts on both replicas, recovered from four faults and two restarts, and drained the pool from about 3 GB to 102 MB.
The measured ref-intake cost is `logs + 2 × edges` round trips at approximately 0.9 ms per trip, making the phase request-bound rather than CPU-bound.
In the measured intake, 7,565 edge reads were re-reads across 4,573 distinct manifests, or 39.6%; all observed re-reads were cross-transaction and none were intra-transaction.

The ref-intake loop is serial: approximately 1.9 million requests at 0.9 ms each imply about 1710 seconds, close to the observed 1830-second maximum and consistent with nearly all phase time being serial request latency.
If the approximately 1710-second serial fetch floor were parallelized N-way, the ideal fetch component would be about 213.75 seconds at N=8 and 106.875 seconds at N=16, before merge cost.

The ref-chain design adds about two serial S3 round trips per committed chunk for `_ckpt`, one conditional PUT per touched namespace per epoch transition during recovery, and one catalog GET per fold round after the hot LIST.
The dominant T15 GC cost was `defer_decision`: 5,096.39 seconds, 79.11% of GC time, including full LISTs of about 177,000 keys even when `changed_shards` was zero.

`CaRetiredInRun_empty_blobs.cfg` and `CaRetiredInRunFoldAbortWitness_empty_blobs.cfg` both passed as green with empty `Blobs` sets.
Across 65,263 ref-log uploads in the affected namespace, partitioned by epoch, zero uploads were out of order.

The GC cadence tradeoff is approximately `A/interval + B·interval`, where `A` is per-fold universe work and `B` is writer amplification from journal growth; the proposed optimal interval scales as `sqrt(U) / r` for blob universe `U` and hottest-shard mutation rate `r`.

GC folds remain O(ref-universe) for large deltas: measured duration grew from about 87 ms at 400 parts to 93 seconds at 10,000 tables and 398 seconds at about 100,000 parts, even though correctness held with `dangling=0`.

The C2 soak comparison recorded 112,518 skipped entries and 110,218 permanently unreachable objects with a cleanup cap of 5000, while disabling the cap drained 223,714 objects with zero unreachable objects.

The `system.cas_gc_log` counters `entries_condemned`, `entries_graduated`, and `entries_redeleted` represent the three retired-cursor pipeline stages: newly condemned, floor-passed and republished `delete_pending`, and executed exact-token blob deletes.
In that fold window, 2,991 manifests carried both an add and a remove edge, and `CasManifestGet == CasRefEmittedEdges`, demonstrating that no manifest-body cache existed.

The outstanding reconciliation debt recorded 56 already-leaked blobs that incremental rounds could never reclaim because their in-degree was pinned above zero; only rebuilding in-degree state could reclaim them.
Before generation retention (B174) was added, a 12h soak measured `gc/` bookkeeping at 82% of pool storage (2822 retained generations, roughly 3.7 MiB/shard/generation), dwarfing actual data 8:1.
GC observability gained per-phase timing during Stage B, which immediately found the fold seal being read five times per round where the design intended two.

The measured GET-cost formula for a folding GC round is exact: total `S3GetObject` = ref-log body GETs + manifest body GETs, i.e. `1 + edges_per_log`, which climbs from 1.54 to 3.73 as backlog grows; round trips equal `logs + edges` at a flat roughly 0.5 ms per round trip across a 140x request range, and a measured 416-round `Success` sample cost roughly $0.007 in total S3 charges.

GC's `fold_ref_intake` is linear in the ref-log backlog at 256 logs/s sustained; the flat cost is per S3 request (~0.92 ms), decomposing as one GET per log body plus one per emitted manifest edge, so round trips equal `logs + 2*edges`, and edges-per-log climbs from 1.54 to 3.73 as backlog grows.

39.6% of GC intake manifest fetches are re-reads (7,565 edges over 4,573 distinct manifests): intra-transaction redundancy is exactly zero, and all of it is cross-transaction (2,991 manifests carry both an add and a remove edge in the window, so the same body is read once when the ref is published and again when it is dropped), making a round-scoped body cache — not an op- or transaction-scoped one — the effective lever.

Probe B's throw wedges GC until an operator runs the rebuild; on a pre-release soak stand this cost a disk-budget blowout, with the last observed run reclaiming 124 GB at one checkpoint once the wedge was cleared, which motivates the open question of whether the first N occurrences should suppress-and-continue with a counter, escalating to a throw only on recurrence.
